closest_works.citation: Hills (2022), Aesthetic testimony, understanding and virtue, sections 5–6
closest_works.shared_claim: Critics' detailed reasons and first-hand engagement can develop one's own aesthetic understanding.
closest_works.difference: Specify when guidance removes an evidential route to checking an audience-relative premise, despite increasing structural understanding; articulate an exception, not refute Hills's qualified typicality claim.

closest_works.citation: Hazlett (2025), Testimony, Understanding, and Art Criticism
closest_works.shared_claim: Explanation can transmit understanding, and testimony is compatible with acquaintance.
closest_works.difference: Disaggregate transmitted structural reasons and response evidence: improvement in understanding of one premise need not reduce, and may increase, dependence regarding another. No denial of testimonial understanding.

closest_works.citation: Johnson, Narratives, Spoilers, and Cooperative Epistemic Environments, early draft
closest_works.shared_claim: Spoilers can remove epistemic benefits; valuable first encounters depend on a cooperative environment.
closest_works.difference: The general epistemic-loss idea is rejected as prior art. Selected increment is a restriction on independent confirmation of a critic's assessment when the offered explanation changes the conditions relevant to its own audience-response premise; applies even to consensual guidance and assessment of failed artistic effects.

closest_works.shared_claim: Narrative form controls attention; retrospective clue visibility differs from uninformed interpretation.
closest_works.difference: This narrative distinction is conceded as known. Proposed new inference is its asymmetrical effect on testimonial dependence and the order of critical instruction.

closest_works.shared_claim: Spoilers concern epistemic autonomy and acquisition of knowledge, not merely pleasure.
closest_works.difference: Selected result concerns evidential confirmation even when explanation is actively requested and welcomed; no general account of spoiler dislike.

limitations: Bounded English web search; several primary works accessed in substantial excerpts rather than entire texts. Hazlett prepublication version used with published metadata; Johnson is an early draft. Levy, Chasid and Molinari direct full-text attempts failed; retrieved excerpts/abstracts retained. Reader-response theory, hindsight bias and aesthetic communication may contain closer antecedents. PASS_RELATIVE is a provisional defended difference for independent precheck, not absolute novelty or draft permission.
